comment: Fleet placement surface registry (docs/placement.md). Adding a location = adding an entry here (+ app installation + a fleet copy). The dispatcher core (tools/fleet-place) reads ONLY this file for what exists; kinds map to adapters in the dispatcher. Limits source: GitHub Actions limits reference, https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits (verified 2026-11-04): concurrent GitHub-hosted jobs per account Free 20 / Pro 40 / Team 60 / Enterprise 500 (macOS subset 5 / 5 / 5 / 50); included private-repo minutes per month Free 2000 / Pro 3000 / Team 3000 / Enterprise 50000; public repositories: minutes unlimited on every plan, so for public targets the binding limit is the concurrency cap, not minutes.

laptop.note: Saturation signal for the codespace tier. Set from pm-dispatch/queue depth where a caller can read it, else flip by hand or pass --laptop-busy. Deliberately not scraped telemetry.

surfaces.notes: Personal copy of the fleet umbrella. Dispatches as the developing-today app via the personal installation (verified 2026-11-04). Repo secrets provisioned (GHCR_ORG_PAT, CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN, NIX_CACHE_SIGNING_KEY, NIX_CACHE_UPLOAD_URL), so cross-repo checkouts work here, and cache pushes will the moment the fork workflow deltas are adopted upstream (upstream fleet-run ignores entry cache fields until then).

Org fork of dezren39/fleet (created 2026-11-04). Actions are enabled at repo level, but the developing-today app installation is repository-selected and does not yet include this repo (API add refused 403; org-owner GUI grant filed under GRANTS NEEDED in the placement report). Ineligible for app dispatch until covered. Also needs repo secrets (GHCR_ORG_PAT for cross-repo checkout; NIX_CACHE_* for cache pushes) before non-trivial jobs.

Third copy of the umbrella, in the forks org (stood up 2026-11-04; Drew is org admin). Absorbed as registry DATA only - no dispatcher change; the live extensibility proof. The developing-today app is NOT installed on developing-today-forks, so this surface is ineligible-app-missing until that grant lands (GRANTS NEEDED); no user-token fallback, per the app-only rule.

Org-level generic runner hosted in the code repo (org-run.yml landed on code main 2026-11-04; runner input parity added by code PR #5417, merged as the app). Dispatches as the app via the org installation. Allowlist = the six org repos in targets.

budget.rate_note: Blacksmith is orgs-only: 3,000 free min/mo, then PAID per-minute (it charges for public-repo minutes past the free tier). paid_cap_minutes is the registry knob Drew can raise; 0 = free tier only.

surfaces.notes: Blacksmith variant of the org fork's fleet-run (runner input = blacksmith, label blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404). Blacksmith app (blacksmith-sh, id 807020) VERIFIED installed on the developing-today org with repository_selection=all (2026-11-04). Org surfaces only — never the personal copy (provider is orgs-only). Inherits fleet-org's app-coverage blocker.

budget.note: Personal Pro Codespaces budget: 180 core-hours/mo. A 4-core codespace burns 4 core-hours per wall hour.

surfaces.notes: Last-resort surface: start/reuse a codespace on the target repo and hand the job to a session inside it. Eligible only when every Actions tier is tapped AND the laptop is saturated (registry laptop.busy or --laptop-busy). Currently pending-scope: gh tokens lack the codespace OAuth scope (gh codespace list returns 403 as of 2026-11-04); the scope grant is being unblocked separately. Reuse-only: fleet-place never creates a codespace; creation stays a deliberate operator act.

The laptop itself (stateful work: deploys, activations, live services) is owned by pm-dispatch/repo-queue lanes, not by fleet-place. This entry exists so a job can PIN the laptop and get a recorded handoff session instead of an Actions run; fleet-place never executes laptop work itself. Saturation input for the spill cascade lives under 'laptop' below.
